acceptance_criteria.criterion: resolve_reviewable_head()'s internal `git log` walk is restricted to first-parent (mainline) history, matching its own docstring's stated intent. Proven by the diff: the only change to scripts/lwb_lanes.py is adding '--first-parent' to that one subprocess.run argv.

The bug is real and observable against this repo's ACTUAL current code (not assumed from the task description): reproduced live in a scratch repo (seed -> substantive -> branch 'side' with one commit touching unrelated.txt -> `git merge --no-ff -s ours side`), where resolve_reviewable_head('HEAD') on the pre-fix code returned the side branch's own commit sha instead of 'substantive'.

A new, deterministic regression test (test_reviewable_head_walks_first_parent_only_not_a_later_dated_side_commit) reproduces this without depending on real-clock timing, by pinning GIT_AUTHOR_DATE/GIT_COMMITTER_DATE so the side commit is dated after the merge. Verified red before the fix (10/10 failures across a loop, after temporarily reverting just the --first-parent addition) and green after (10/10 passes), confirming the test is not timing-lucky.

The pre-existing test_is_record_only_commit_true_for_a_merge_with_empty_first_parent_diff (added by #56) is unaffected by this fix and still passes -- run 15x in a loop with the fix applied, all green. It was also confirmed to pass 20/20 WITHOUT the fix on this machine (real-clock timestamps, commits made milliseconds apart), consistent with the task's own description of it as timing/platform-dependent rather than deterministically red on every platform -- which is exactly why the new deterministic test above was added rather than relying on that one alone.

commit_files()'s own first-parent diffing of merge commits (added by #56) is unmodified and still correctly complements this fix rather than conflicting with it -- confirmed by the diff touching nothing in commit_files() or _is_record_only_commit(), and by the full test suite (including all of #56's merge-handling tests) passing unmodified.

commits_in_range() (a different `git log --format=%H` call, for enumerating every commit in a base..head range for per-commit identity/lane checks) is deliberately left untouched -- not confident --first-parent is correct there too, given it may be meant to include commits merged in from a side branch. Noted as an open question in the PR body rather than guessed at, per instruction.
